key_insight: Using a log-barrier regularizer inside an online mirror-descent style algorithm, together with a dual-focused analysis, yields optimal last-iterate convergence for uncoupled zero-sum matrix games under bandit feedback — matching the known Omega(t^{-1/4}) lower bound.
problem_solved: How to learn minimax policies in zero-sum matrix games with only bandit (partial) feedback while guaranteeing fast, last-iterate convergence for uncoupled players — a setting where prior methods failed to attain the optimal rate.
method: Incorporate a log-barrier regularizer into a mirror-descent/online-learning update to keep iterates well-conditioned near the simplex boundary.
Develop a dual-focused convergence analysis that directly controls last-iterate exploitability (rather than averaged iterates) and matches the lower bound.
Design bandit-friendly gradient estimators and exploration/step-size choices (importance-weighting / variance control) to operate with partial payoff observations.
impact: Provides a practical, theoretically optimal algorithm for multi-agent and adversarial learning tasks with limited feedback, enabling more stable and faster-converging strategies in applications like multi-agent RL, online auctions, and adversarial training.
visual_elements: Log-barrier update schematic: diagram showing simplex, iterates, and how log-barrier prevents boundary collapse.
Convergence plot: log-log chart comparing last-iterate exploitability rates (achieved Θ(t^{-1/4}) vs slower baselines and the lower bound).
Bandit feedback flow: two-player diagram showing limited payoff observation and importance-weighted gradient estimation.
Upper vs lower bound panel: simple bar/line graphic illustrating the prior Ω(t^{-1/4}) lower bound and this paper's matching upper bound.
paper_title: Optimal last-iterate convergence in matrix games with bandit feedback using the log-barrier
paper_authors: Come Fiegel, Pierre Menard, Tadashi Kozuno, Michal Valko, Vianney Perchet
